label: org.ent.radiostation.radio-liberty
description: US-funded international broadcaster directed at audiences in the Soviet Union. Founded in 1951 by the American Committee for the Liberation of the Peoples of Russia (Amcomlib). Initially known as Radio Liberation from Bolshevism and later Radio Liberation before adopting the name Radio Liberty. It operated separately from Radio Free Europe until their merger in 1976.
annotation_note: Annotate Radio Liberty, Radio-Liberty, Radio Liberation, and related historical forms when they refer to the broadcaster, a broadcast source, a programme, a transmission, or institutional radio activity. Do not normalize Radio Liberty to Radio Free Europe in pre-1976 contexts; they were separate broadcasters.

active_period.note: Founded in 1951. Began broadcasting in 1953. Merged with Radio Free Europe in 1976 to form Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty.

label: org.ent.radiostation.polskie-radio
description: Polish public radio broadcaster founded in 1925. Historical newspapers frequently refer to broadcasts from Warsaw using translated station names such as Radio Varsovie, Radio Warsaw, Radio Warschau, Warschauer Rundfunk, or Sender Warschau. In news reports, programme listings, source attributions, and broadcast announcements these forms typically refer to the Polish Radio network rather than a separate broadcaster entity.
annotation_note: Annotate Polskie Radio and historical station forms such as Radio Varsovie, Radio Warsaw, Radio Warschau, Warschauer Rundfunk, and Sender Warschau when the context refers to a broadcaster, broadcast source, programme listing, transmission, radio announcement, or institutional radio activity. Normalize these forms to org.ent.radiostation.polskie-radio.

active_period.note: Polskie Radio was established in 1925. Regular broadcasting from Warsaw began in April 1926 and became the core station of the national Polish radio network.

label: org.ent.radiostation.bbc
description: British public broadcaster. In wartime European newspaper contexts, names such as Radio Londres, Radio London, Radio Londra, and Londoner Rundfunk usually refer to BBC foreign-language broadcasts from London rather than to separate stations. These broadcasts could involve Free French, exile-government, resistance, or other allied contributors, but the broadcasting infrastructure and service were part of the BBC's wider European output.
annotation_note: Normalize wartime foreign-language references to Radio Londres/Radio London/Radio Londra/Londoner Rundfunk to org.ent.radiostation.bbc when the context is a broadcast, source attribution, programme, or broadcaster mention.

label: org.ent.radiostation.radio-bucharest
description: Romanian international/state broadcaster from Bucharest. In French and German historical newspaper snippets, Radio Bucarest or Radio-Bucarest is used as a broadcast-source name for announcements from Bucharest. Radio Romania International documents that in 1948 broadcasts in French, English, Russian, Serbian, and German were aired from Bucharest, and that Radio Bucharest later became Radio Romania International.
annotation_note: Annotate Radio Bucarest/Radio-Bucarest as a radio-station or broadcaster mention when it introduces, reports, announces, schedules, or otherwise refers to a broadcast/media-source function.

active_period.note: Foreign-language programming from Bucharest began in 1932; Radio Bucharest became Radio Romania International after 1989.

label: org.ent.radiostation.deutsche-welle
description: German broadcaster name covering both the modern international broadcaster founded in 1953 and its historical predecessor name Deutsche Welle GmbH, founded in 1924 and broadcasting from 1926 via the long-wave Deutschlandsender at Königs Wusterhausen. Historical programme listings from the 1920s and early 1930s may print station forms such as Deutsche Welle-Königswusterhausen.
annotation_note: Annotate Deutsche Welle in modern international-broadcasting contexts and in 1920s/1930s programme listings referring to the earlier Deutsche Welle GmbH/Deutschlandsender service. Include hyphenated station-location suffixes such as Deutsche Welle-Königswusterhausen when visibly attached.

active_period.note: Historical Deutsche Welle GmbH was founded in 1924, began regular broadcasting in 1926, and was renamed Deutschlandsender GmbH in 1933. Modern Deutsche Welle was founded in 1953.

label: org.ent.radiostation.rfi
description: Canonical umbrella entity for France's public international broadcasting service from the creation of Poste Colonial in 1931 through the present Radio France Internationale. The service successively appeared under historical names including Poste Colonial, Paris-Mondial, and external services of RTF/ORTF before the Radio France Internationale name was introduced on 6 January 1975. RFI became an independent national broadcasting company in 1987 and has belonged to France Médias Monde since 2008.
annotation_note: Use org.ent.radiostation.rfi as the canonical label for the continuous French public international broadcasting lineage from 1931 onward, while preserving the historical visible name as the annotated surface. This includes clearly identified international-service mentions of Poste Colonial, Paris-Mondial, RTF Radio Paris, and ORTF Radio Paris, as well as RFI and Radio France Internationale from 1975 onward. Bare Radio Paris remains ambiguous and requires explicit French external-service context; do not globally normalize every Radio Paris mention to RFI.

active_period.note: Canonical coverage begins with Poste Colonial in 1931. The Radio France Internationale name was introduced on 6 January 1975; RFI became an independent national programme company in 1987 and remains active under France Médias Monde.

label: org.ent.radiostation.rts
description: Swiss public broadcaster for French-speaking Switzerland. Radio Suisse Romande (RSR), founded in 1922 as a radio unit of SRG SSR, merged with Télévision Suisse Romande in 2010 to form Radio Télévision Suisse (RTS), covering radio, television, and online services.

active_period.note: Radio Suisse Romande existed as RSR until the 2010 merger; the continuing broadcaster is Radio Télévision Suisse (RTS).

label: org.ent.radiostation.vatican-radio
aliases: radio de la Cité du Vatican
Radio de la Cité du Vatican
radio de la Cite du Vatican
Radio de la Cite du Vatican
description: International radio service of the Holy See and Vatican City, inaugurated in 1931. Historical newspapers may refer to it by translated station names such as Radio Vatican, Radio Vatikan, Radio Vaticano, or Radio Vaticana in news/source and programme contexts.
annotation_note: Annotate translated forms such as Radio Vatican, Radio Vatikan, Radio Vaticano, and Radio Vaticana as Vatican Radio when the context refers to the broadcaster, a broadcast, a programme, or a source attribution.

active_period.note: Vatican Radio began regular broadcasting in 1931 and continues as part of Vatican media services.

label: org.ent.radiostation.rtl
description: Luxembourg-based multilingual commercial broadcaster launched in 1933 and widely known as Radio Luxembourg; in many non-English contexts the broadcaster was known as RTL, from Radio Télévision Luxembourg. The historical English-language Radio Luxembourg service ended in 1992, while related RTL radio and television brands continue under the RTL broadcaster/media group.

active_period.note: Historical Radio Luxembourg service launched in 1933; the English-language service ended in 1992, while related RTL radio/television broadcaster brands continue.
